specificationName: Activity System Runtime Validation with Complete Log Confirmation

validationResults.input: Create a test file named quicktest.txt
validationResults.expected: All 8 lifecycle log patterns visible in kubectl logs output
validationResults.actual: 0/8 patterns found. Activity system not triggered - simple tool call executed instead. Lifecycle logs not visible in kubectl logs.
validationResults.difference: Test prompt too simple, did not trigger activity execution. OpenCode handled as direct Write tool call instead of activity template. kubectl exec subprocess logs are isolated from pod logs (kubectl logs shows only main ACP server process).

diagnostics.commandExecuted: kubectl exec -n metabob devbob-794b69b4f4-rhnwg -- sh -c 'echo "Create a test file named quicktest.txt" | opencode run'
diagnostics.podLogsCheck: Only ACP server startup logs visible, no activity execution logs
diagnostics.execStderr: Service initialization logs, no lifecycle patterns
diagnostics.rootCause: Activity recommendation system not triggered by simple prompt

validationResults.reason: Test Case 1 revealed architectural issue - kubectl exec logs isolated from pod logs
Test Case 1 revealed need for activity-triggering prompts or ACP API usage

criticalFindings.description: Simple prompts are handled as direct tool calls, bypassing activity system
criticalFindings.impact: Lifecycle logs never generated because activity execution never started
criticalFindings.recommendation: Use complex multi-step prompts or direct activity invocation via opencode activity run

criticalFindings.description: Subprocess logs from kubectl exec are isolated from main pod process logs
criticalFindings.impact: Even if activity executed, lifecycle logs would not appear in kubectl logs output
criticalFindings.recommendation: Execute activities via ACP API (HTTP) to main process, making logs visible in kubectl logs

criticalFindings.description: Specification assumes kubectl logs captures activity logs, but architecture uses subprocess execution
criticalFindings.impact: Validation methodology incompatible with current deployment architecture
criticalFindings.recommendation: Update validation to use ACP API or accept exec stderr as valid log source

recommendedActions.example: Analyze the codebase, identify patterns, create documentation, and commit changes
recommendedActions.rationale: Complex multi-step tasks trigger activity recommendation system
Bypasses recommendation system, forces activity execution

recommendedActions.implementation: HTTP POST to ACP server instead of kubectl exec
recommendedActions.rationale: Makes lifecycle logs visible in main process (kubectl logs)

recommendedActions.change: Accept kubectl exec stderr as valid log source

conclusionSummary: Validation harness infrastructure complete (100%). Validation execution failed (0/8 patterns) due to: (1) Test prompt too simple, didn't trigger activity system, (2) kubectl exec subprocess logs isolated from pod logs, (3) Specification assumed kubectl logs would show activity logs, but requires main process execution via ACP API. Lifecycle logging IS implemented in source code (verified commit 305a9ab6). Failure is methodological, not functional.
